newsitem.title: BRAZIL: JP Morgan Brazil sees $68 mln 1996 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan Brazil sees $68 mln 1996 oper profit.

text.p: U.S. investment bank J.P. Morgan's Brazilian units expect to post a consolidated operating profit of $67.99 million this year, up from $53.2 million in 1995, the bank's Brazil chief said.
"We had a good year (and) expect that will continue" in 1997, said Alfredo Gutierrez, the bank's managing director for Mercosur and president of Brazil operations.
He told reporters that the rise in operating profit was due mostly to a $100 million capital injection this year and Brazil's improving economy.

J.P. Morgan's Brazil operations also expect to close 1996 with a net worth of $236.4 million, up from $124.8 million last year, and total assets of $1.58 billion versus $1.4 billion, according to bank figures.
The bank's Brazil operations are comprised of Morgan Guaranty Trust Co of New York's Sao Paulo branch, Banco J.P. Morgan S.A. and brokerage JPM Corretora de Titulos e Valores Mobiliarios S.A.
The Brazil unit acted as advisor or underwriter in six mergers and acquisitions in 1996.
